7. Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed, learned Counsel appearing for the plaintiff—respondents, drew our attention to the lower Appellate Court's judgment for coming to the conclusion, (i) that the plaintiff opposite party has been possessing the suit land since her purchase by kabala dated 7.2.1975, (ii) that Gopal Chandra She did not leave this country and he was a Bangladeshi National in the year 1975 when the kabala was executed and registered, (iii) defendant No. 1-2 never got possession of the suit land, (iv) presumption is attached by law under section 60 of the Registration Act that the plaintiffs vendor was physically present in Bangladesh and lastly (v) injunction prayer was granted rightly re-straining defendant No. 1 from leasing out of the suit land treating it as enemy property. Mr. Ahmed argued that the aforesaid findings have been arrived at on evidence and there is no scope for a remand order. He submitted further that leave was granted on a point which has become academic now because the point has been settled by this Court in M/s. Dulichand Omraolal case. 

 8. The submission of Mr. Khondker Mahbubuddin Ahmed has considerable force. The legal aspect of the matter has been settled already and Mr. Moksudur Rahman also does not dispute this proposition. Therefore Mr. Moksudur Rahman argued forcefully for remand. But a remand order is not to be granted as a matter of routine. Section 29 ALL 184 P.C. and 17 ALL 112 P.C. Mr. Moksudur Rahman found it difficult to pinpoint the area of investigation which could be done on remand. The crucial question is as to the physical presence of the vendor. It is presumed under section 60 that the registration was done in accordance with law and the requirement of the law was fulfilled. It is a rebuttable presumption, no doubt, but Mr. Moksudur Rahman could not argue, how the evidence as it is, has rebutted the presumption. The defendants got ample opportunity at the trial stage and no such rebuttal evidence was adduced. Hence the prayer for remand does not merit consideration. Since the point has been settled already on which the leave was granted, Mr. Ahmed is correct in saying the appeal has become of mere academic interest.
